ai.definition: CO2-Mineralized Concrete is a type of cementitious material where carbon dioxide (CO2) is chemically bound during its production and curing process, forming stable calcium carbonate minerals within the concrete structure.
ai.howItWorks: The CO2 is injected into the concrete mix in a liquid or supercritical state. As the concrete cures, the CO2 reacts with the cementitious materials to form calcium carbonate (CaCO3) minerals, effectively storing the CO2 within the concrete's microstructure over time.
ai.problemSolved: This technology addresses the issue of CO2 emissions from the construction sector by permanently sequestering CO2 during the production and curing process of concrete. It also reduces reliance on traditional cement, which has a significant carbon footprint.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves mixing conventional concrete materials with captured CO2 before pouring and setting the mixture into forms or molds.
ai.buildProcess: After the concrete sets, it undergoes a curing process where the CO2 is chemically bound to form calcium carbonate minerals. This process can take several days to weeks depending on the environmental conditions.
ai.costDrivers: The primary cost drivers include the capture and transportation of CO2, the additional energy required for the injection process, and potentially higher material costs due to specialized equipment or additives used in the mix.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is positive as the technology has shown promising results in pilot projects. However, widespread adoption will depend on further scaling and cost reduction efforts.
ai.regulation: Current regulations are fragmented, with some regions offering incentives for CO2 sequestration technologies but lacking specific standards or guidelines for CO2-mineralized concrete.
ai.risks: Technical risks include the stability of CO2 mineralization over time in different environmental conditions. Economic risks involve the high initial costs and potential market acceptance issues.
ai.profitability: Profitability is currently uncertain due to the nascent stage of the technology and the need for further cost reductions and market validation.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on optimizing the CO2 mineralization process, reducing manufacturing energy requirements, and scaling up production capabilities.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking. The overall energy intensity can be reduced through process optimization and the use of renewable energy sources.

glossary.def: A state of carbon dioxide where it exists between its liquid and gas phases, allowing for efficient injection into concrete mixes.
Materials that set and harden by reacting with water, including cement and other binders used in concrete production.

subsystems.name: Binder
subsystems.role: the reactive cement phases that will combine with CO2 to form solid carbonate.
parts: supplementary cementitious materials such as slag or fly ash

subsystems.name: CO2 supply and dosing
subsystems.role: delivers purified, liquefied CO2 into the mixer at a controlled rate.

subsystems.name: Batching and mixing
subsystems.role: where aggregate, binder, water, admixtures and CO2 are combined.

subsystems.name: Curing system
subsystems.role: either normal moist curing of ready-mix, or a CO2-rich chamber for precast units.

subsystems.name: Mineralization chemistry
subsystems.role: dissolved CO2 forms carbonate ions that precipitate as calcium carbonate inside the pore structure.

subsystems.name: Testing and accounting
subsystems.role: proves the concrete still meets strength and durability specs, and quantifies how much CO2 is locked in.

buildSteps.title: Capture the CO2
buildSteps.detail: A stream of high-purity CO2 is separated at an industrial plant — often an ethanol, ammonia or gas-processing facility, where the gas is already concentrated. Cement kiln flue gas is dilute and needs more processing.

buildSteps.title: Purify and deliver
buildSteps.detail: The gas is dried, compressed or liquefied, and shipped by tanker or pipeline to the concrete plant.

buildSteps.title: Batch the mix
buildSteps.detail: Sand, crushed rock, cement, water, admixtures and any supplementary materials are weighed and loaded into the mixer using an established mix design.

buildSteps.title: Inject and mix
buildSteps.detail: A metered dose of CO2 is fed into the drum during mixing. It dissolves, reacts with calcium in the binder, and precipitates fine calcium carbonate particles that fill pores and add early strength.

buildSteps.title: Place the concrete
buildSteps.detail: The mixture is poured, pumped or cast into forms while still workable — the reaction must be tuned so it does not stiffen the mix too early.

buildSteps.title: Cure
buildSteps.detail: Ready-mix cures conventionally while the mineralized carbonate stays locked in the matrix. Precast blocks, pavers and pipes can instead cure in a sealed chamber flooded with CO2, which reacts across the whole surface.

buildSteps.title: Test and release
buildSteps.detail: Cylinders are crushed to confirm strength and samples are analysed for carbonate content, so the producer can certify both performance and stored CO2.

buildSteps.title: Operate and account
buildSteps.detail: The concrete goes into pavements, foundations, walls and pipes, where the carbonate remains stable for the life of the structure — and even after demolition, if the rubble is not recarbonated away.

prerequisites.why: the feedstock has to come from somewhere; today it comes mainly from already-concentrated industrial streams.
concrete plants need consistent, dry, metered CO2 rather than raw flue gas.
dosing must be precise; too little does nothing and too much harms workability.

prerequisites.tech: Standards and verification for CO2 storage in concrete
prerequisites.why: buyers and regulators need agreed methods to count and audit the carbon that is genuinely mineralized.
stored CO2 is only a small fraction of concrete's footprint — the far bigger gain is cutting the cement content it is blended into.

pathway.milestone: CO2 injection during mixing at commercial ready-mix plants, and CO2 curing of precast blocks and pavers
pathway.unlocks: a modest but real emissions cut per cubic metre plus a strength benefit, and a business case that needs no subsidy for the gas itself.

pathway.milestone: carbonation of recycled concrete aggregate and crushed demolition waste
pathway.unlocks: a way to store CO2 in material that would otherwise be landfilled, and to improve recycled aggregate quality.

pathway.milestone: combination with low-clinker binders and alternative cements
pathway.unlocks: much larger emission reductions, with mineralization handling the residual carbon that cannot be designed out.

pathway.milestone: designed-in carbonation of the whole concrete life cycle, including end-of-life rubble
pathway.unlocks: concrete acting as a durable, verifiable carbon sink rather than only a source.
